project_tracker_diagnostic: Perennial thistle with strongly wavy/lobed leaves and dense gray-white tomentum beneath; large purple heads; often more woolly than Texas thistle.

project_inclusion.learning_reason: Common, conspicuous, or high-value comparison species for Central Texas field ID.

morphology_keys.leaves: Cauline leaves mainly ovate to lanceolate, often entire or coarsely toothed or shallowly lobed (variable); gray-white wool on lower face. A strongly wavy margin is NOT universal or a single-species proof.
morphology_keys.heads: Large purple discoid heads, usually on evident peduncles.
morphology_keys.phyllaries: Lanceolate and spine-tipped; larger involucres can exceed 3 cm.
best_field_traits: Broader ovate/lanceolate upper stem leaves: unlobed/coarsely toothed/shallowly lobed in FNA key.
Lower leaf surfaces woolly gray-white; gray color alone shared with ochrocentrum and western Cirsium.
Outer/mid phyllaries may have a longitudinal glutinous resin ridge, seen best by wet/dry macro.
Involucres of larger heads often >30 mm; photograph without corolla with ruler.
Mature cypselae about 6–7 mm long; apical collar roughly same color as fruit body.
Contrast C. ochrocentrum with stronger phyllary spines and decurrent wings in some forms; avoid absolute wing-only key.

photo_strategy.selection_logic: Prefer curated taxon photos plus multiple views from one Central Texas/Texas observation.

look_here_first: Inspect full MID-STEM leaf shape and its TWO surfaces, then the SIDE of the involucre. C. undulatum tends to have gray-white wool beneath and relatively broader ovate/lanceolate stem leaves that are entire, coarse-toothed or shallowly lobed (not necessarily deeply feather-cut). In larger heads the involucre is often >3 cm; inspect a resinous/glutinous ridge down outer/middle phyllary midveins. For hard undulatum vs ochrocentrum calls, mature cypselae ~6–7 mm with body and rim same color, plus leaf division and wing extent, are useful.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Undulatum: broader subentire to shallowly lobed cauline leaves, woolly undersides, often large involucre, mature cypselae ~6–7 mm with concolorous apical rim. Ochrocentrum may have conspicuous decurrent spiny stem wings, longer phyllary spine tips and woolly herbage; forms overlap. Vulgare shows unique short bristle-spines on upper leaf blade. Texanum has considerably smaller involucres.
